text:
mike_dev: heads up - saw user emails slip through logs in the node sampleapp when auth retries kick in. seems like the redaction hook runs too early.
anya: ugh. can you paste the tiny log excerpt? node or go sample?
mike_dev: node. here's a short tail from my run:
```
INFO  req.start - req_id=orig-001 user=redacted@example.com
DEBUG auth.retry - req_id=orig-001 attempt=2 status=401
INFO  handler - req_id=retry-002 user=leak@example.com action=proxy
```
ben_platform: looks like retry mutates the request id and some middleware snapshots headers before the final state. our redact hook is attached at request init.
jen_sre: if middleware captures sensitive fields on attach, any header mutation later will bypass scrub. two options: 1) redact at emit time (recommended), 2) ensure redact middleware runs after retry middleware.
mike_dev: for tracing we do want a stable original_request_id across attempts. devs also expect a deterministic req_id for correlation.
anya: solution idea - expose both ids in logs: original_req_id + attempt_id. redaction should run in the logger transport using the live context. add SDK config redactOnEmit: true by default for new versions.
ben_platform: implemented a quick local patch to move redaction into the logger's beforeSend hook and kept original_req_id in context. diff snippet:
```diff
- logHook.scrubOnAttach(ctx)
+ logHook.on('beforeSend', (entry) => {
+   const ctx = getRuntimeContext(entry)
+   scrubSensitive(ctx)
+ })
```
ben_platform: that removed the raw email from my retry stress test.
jen_sre: great. small concern: some customers explicitly parse headers in middleware expecting redacted values earlier. we should document the change and add an opt-out.
mike_dev: i'll open a PR with the middleware reorder + the emit-time scrub option and a mocha test that simulates 401 -> 200 retry.
anya: add a flag in sampleapp config: preserveLegacyRedactBehavior = true/false to make migrations smoother. also add telemetry counter metric: telemetry.unredacted_email_detected.
jen_sre: i'll write the mocha test and a quick e2e that asserts the metric stays zero after canary.
ci-bot: CI triggered for branch fix/redact-emit (build #9032).
ci-bot: unit tests passed (20s).
mike_dev: PR up: moves redact to emit + adds original_req_id/attempt_id fields + config flag + test. ping for review.
anya: reviewing now. small nit: update README sample logging pattern to include both ids and explain why emit-time is safer.
ben_platform: note: make sure json logger still redacts nested JSON payloads that may contain PII; transport-level scrub needs to traverse payloads.
jen_sre: added that to test matrix. also document the caveat about customers doing early header-based scrubbing.
mike_dev: thanks — once merged let's run a short staging canary and watch the unredacted_email metric for 2h.
anya: agreed. rolling canary after merge. :rocket:
ci-bot: build #9032 deployed to staging canary.
jen_sre: initial canary metrics look clean, no unredacted hits. closing once 2h holds.
mike_dev: closing thread for now, will reopen if algo shows up. :thumbsup:
